properties.name: OBSERVED 2026-09-29: export_graph reported `wrote: unchanged` for a write that DID change the file, because only prev_content_hash moved (the chain anchor changed after merging main into a branch)
properties.source: shipping PR #622 in the dev_reflow2 hub session, reflow2 0.74.0 + branch build
properties.statement:
Observed while merging main (#621) into feat/a-stored-twin-has-one-authority.
- The first export was written before the merge commit existed, so it chained from the OLD merge-base (329a074) and recorded that export's hash as its prev_content_hash.
- After the merge commit, the same store was exported again. The receipt said chained_from origin/main@686b955 and `wrote: unchanged`.
- Yet `git status` showed the file modified: exactly one line, prev_content_hash, moved from 329a074's export hash to 686b955's.
- The gate (reflow2_check LINEAGE) read the committed copy, which still had the old anchor, and failed.

Expected: `wrote: changed` whenever the file's bytes change, lineage fields included. The tool description says to READ `wrote`, because the hashes cannot tell a no-op from a save.

Not established: whether `wrote` compares content_hash only (which excludes lineage) rather than the bytes written. No cause is claimed. The workaround used: export only after the merge commit exists, and read git status rather than `wrote`.
